tldr: CISA adds major Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerability to KEV catalog with immediate federal patching mandate.
Anthropic releases Claude 4.5, demonstrating significant improvements in multi-step reasoning and cybersecurity research capabilities.
Major retail breach affects over 2 million records; data allegedly exfiltrated via compromised third-party vendor credentials.

ai.prose: The AI landscape shifted significantly this week with the release of Claude 4.5. The new model exhibits a marked decrease in hallucination rates when processing technical documentation, a critical metric for security analysts using LLMs for code review. Meanwhile, the EU AI Act's technical standards committee has begun drafting specific requirements for general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, focusing on transparency in training data. This move signal a transition from broad policy to enforceable technical controls. We are also seeing a rise in 'agentic' security tools that leverage these models to automate initial triage, though reliability in high-stakes environments remains a topic of intense debate among practitioners.

cybersecurity.policy_prose: CISA has issued a rare Emergency Directive (ED 26-01) following the widespread exploitation of the Ivanti vulnerability. Federal agencies are required to disconnect affected instances within 24 hours. This follows a similar move by the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC), indicating a coordinated Five Eyes response. At the industry level, the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) has announced new funding for critical infrastructure projects to implement memory-safe languages, specifically targeting legacy networking equipment.
